text:
maya: Quick check — running into a helm override precedence weirdness when deploying via Terraform's helm_release.
maya: Subchart's deployment uses an env var like:
```yaml
- name: EXTERNAL_API_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secrets.apiKeyName }}
      key: api_key
```
maya: I'm passing a set from Terraform like: `set { name = "global.secrets.apiKeyName" value = "myapp-api-{{terraform.workspace}}" }` but the rendered manifest still shows the old secret name from chart defaults.
sam: hmm — a couple quick things: are you using `values = [file("values.yaml")]` as well? set can be tripped by precedence ordering. Also share the chart's values.yml snippet and how the subchart references `secrets` (is it under `global` or local)?
maya: I have a values file in the repo with `secrets:
  apiKeyName: chart-default-secret` and the subchart expects `.Values.secrets.apiKeyName` (not `.Values.global.secrets`).
jordan: If the subchart expects `.Values.secrets` you need to either set that path directly (`secrets.apiKeyName`) or move it to `global.secrets` and have the subchart read `$.Values.global.secrets`. Helm's merge semantics mean subchart/local value takes precedence unless the chart explicitly reads `global`.
jordan: Also Terraform helm_release has subtlety: `values = [...]` are loaded and then `set`/`set_string` are applied. If you pass the same key in both a file and `set`, `set` should override — but if the subchart is using a different path (`global` vs local) they won't map.
leo: another gotcha — if your secret name itself contains templates (eg `myapp-secret-{{ .Release.Namespace }}`) the chart must use `tpl` to render that string at template time: `{{ tpl .Values.secrets.apiKeyName . }}` otherwise it will literally render `{{ .Release.Namespace }}`.
maya: aha — we actually template the name in values: `apiKeyName: "myapp-{{ .Release.Namespace }}-api"` and I didn't realize `tpl` was required. Could that be why our override still shows the old literal?
jordan: yes. Use `tpl` where the value is intended to be rendered as a template. Example in deployment: `name: {{ tpl .Values.secrets.apiKeyName . }}`.
sam: quick checklist to debug: 
- run `helm template ./chart -f values.yaml --set global.secrets.apiKeyName=...` locally to inspect rendered name
- compare `values` vs `set` in your Terraform helm_release block; try putting the override in `values` file to test parity
- `kubectl get secret` in the namespace after deploy — if you're using ExternalSecret CRD, note that the secret may be created async by controller (pod will wait).
leo: related: if you rely on ExternalSecret to create the secret, the helm chart might want to create an ExternalSecret resource (not a core Secret). The ExternalSecret controller will generate the Secret later, so during unit tests `required` checks can fail. Avoid `required` for cross-resource timing; instead fail fast in CI that renders templates (use `helm template`).
infra-bot: deploy queued for maya/test -> cluster-prod in 5m (dry-run enabled) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya: thanks all. Plan: 1) try `tpl` fix in deployment template, 2) move override to `global.secrets.apiKeyName` and update Terraform `set` to match, 3) `helm template` locally to confirm. I'll post rendered snippet after trying.
sam: ping me if you want me to test the terraform plan/apply flow — I can try a local `helm template` with your values first.
maya: will do. Thanks :thumbsup:
